ov: A duck-billed, egg-laying mammal of eastern Australia and Tasmania. It hunts underwater with its eyes, ears and nostrils shut, finding prey through electroreceptors in its bill.

why.dg: Males have a spur on each hind foot that delivers venom, strong enough to cause severe pain and swelling in people.
why.ac: Mainly nocturnal, but also active at dusk in summer and during the day in winter.

rg: Rivers and streams of eastern Australia, including Tasmania.
df: Insect larvae, worms, shrimp, crayfish, small shellfish, tadpoles and fish eggs, stored in its cheek pouches while it forages.

cf.tip: The only other egg-laying mammals are the four species of echidna, which are covered in spines and live on land.

fx: When scientists first examined one, in 1799, they thought it was a fake made of several animals sewn together.
